name: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine (T-DM1)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate (trastuzumab linked to emtansine, a microtubule inhibitor): requires HER2-positive disease (IHC 3+ or ISH-amplified). Per DeVita 12th ed. and Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer.

histology: invasive breast carcinoma (histology-agnostic; includes invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) and invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC))
supportiveCare: Antiemetics: low-to-moderate emetic risk; prophylaxis per emetogenicity tier.
Cardiac: evaluate LVEF before and during HER2-targeted therapy (BINV-M 1 of 10).
Monitor platelets (thrombocytopenia) and hepatic transaminases (transaminitis) each cycle per DeVita adverse-event profile (line 21439).

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 to 4 thrombocytopenia or significant transaminase elevation
doseModificationRules.text: Hold or dose-reduce per labeling for thrombocytopenia or hepatotoxicity; obtain clinical review. DeVita reports thrombocytopenia 12.8% and transient transaminitis 4.3% (line 21439).

drugs.name: Ado-trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., ado-trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (every 21 days) for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (lines 20796 to 20802; 21438). Concordant with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v6.2026 metastatic dosing (T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV day 1, every 21 days, BINV-Q 10 of 15). Do not confuse with fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan; do not substitute trastuzumab and hyaluronidase-oysk for this agent.

provenance.locator: lines 20796 to 20802 (drug table: ado-trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg IV every 3 wk, HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer); line 21438 (dosed at 3.6 mg/kg IV every 21 days)
